args.text: [lane-marten] Three risks of caching DNS answers too long: (1) Stale records: clients keep resolving to old IPs after failover, migration, or decommissioning, causing outages or misrouting. (2) Slow security response: if a domain is hijacked, poisoned, or repointed to fix a compromise, bad answers persist in caches well past the fix. (3) Delayed change propagation: rollouts, cutovers, and certificate/endpoint changes take longer and behave inconsistently across resolvers, and traffic may reach dangling or reassigned IPs (raising takeover risk).

[lane-marten] Idempotent retries matter because networks and services fail in ambiguous ways, so a client often can't tell whether a request succeeded and must retry to be reliable. If the operation is idempotent, repeating it yields the same result as doing it once, so retries can't cause duplicate charges, double writes, or other corrupted state.

[lane-marten] Two trade-offs of UUIDv7 as a primary key: (1) Size and readability: at 16 bytes it is larger than a 4- or 8-byte integer key, so indexes and foreign keys take more space and are harder to read and debug, though its time-ordered prefix gives much better insert locality than random UUIDv4. (2) Information leakage and weaker ordering guarantees: the embedded millisecond timestamp reveals when a record was created, and ordering is only approximate across nodes (clock skew, same-millisecond ties), so it is not a strict sequence.
